subject: SLA template variance proposal — monthly credit bands & latency SLOs
messages:
From: Rajesh Patel <rajesh.patel@borealis.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@borealis.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0500
Subject: SLA template variance request — uptime bands & monthly credits

Hi Irene / Aditya,

Thank you again for the demo last week. We’re nearing internal procurement sign-off, but legal has flagged Redwood’s standard SLA credit structure. A couple of asks from our side:

- We need a narrower monthly availability band around the 99.9% mark and clearer examples of how monthly service credits are calculated.
- Because our workload is latency-sensitive during business hours, can you include a latency SLO (p99 response within 220ms for text-generation endpoints) and an associated credit table?
- We’d like the monthly credit cap increased slightly from the standard language to allow up to 100% of monthly fees in rare sustained outages while limiting perpetual exposure.

I’ve attached our proposed redlines to the template (borealis_sla_redlines_v1.docx). We’re sensitive to keeping procurement timelines short — if possible, can we get an initial Redwood proposal by end of next week?

Thanks,
Rajesh
Head of Procurement
Borealis Systems

[Attachment: borealis_sla_redlines_v1.docx (docx)]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Patel <rajesh.patel@borealis.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: SLA template variance request — uptime bands & monthly credits

Rajesh — thanks for the clear note and the attachment. Looping in Aditya (sales), Laura (legal) and Marissa (CS) so we can align on a pragmatic template variant.

Quick initial position from product/ops perspective: we can create a limited SLA variant that adds an explicit latency SLO for your primary text-generation route and a clarified credit calculation example. A few practical guardrails we’d propose:

- Baseline availability remains 99.9% monthly for the Hosted API footprint that Borealis will consume; an alternate banding can be applied for the first 12 months post-onboarding as a pilot.
- Proposed credit bands (example):
  • 99.9% — no credit
  • 99.5%–99.9% — 10% of monthly invoice
  • 99.0%–99.49% — 25% of monthly invoice
  • <99.0% — 50% of monthly invoice

- Latency SLO (p99): 220ms for text-generation (business-hours), with credits tiered separately: 5% for p99 >220ms up to 300ms; 15% for p99 >300ms up to 450ms; 30% for p99 >450ms. Credits are calculated independently but capped as below.

- Cap and duration: we can agree to a temporary uplift on the credit cap for the first 12 months (up to 100% of the monthly fee in extreme, sustained incidents), but we prefer a hard aggregate cap equal to three months' charges over any 12-month rolling window rather than an uncapped lifetime exposure.

- Maintenance carveouts: regular maintenance windows (announced 72+ hours in advance) and emergency maintenance validated by our ops team will be excluded from availability calculations.

I’ll let Laura propose the legal language/limits and Aditya confirm commercial implications. If these guardrails look sensible, we’ll draft a formal SLA variant (redwood_sla_variant_proposal.pdf) and include example calculations.

Best,
Irene
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood_sla_variant_proposal.pdf (pdf)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2026 08:31:00 -0500
Subject: Re: SLA template variance request — uptime bands & monthly credits

Rajesh — appreciate the prompt. A couple of commercial notes from our side to keep procurement timelines moving:

- We’re comfortable with the temporary uplift to the credit ceiling for a 12-month pilot tied to the initial committed capacity. After the pilot, we’d revert to the standard cap (three months aggregate across a 12-month rolling period).
- To protect both sides financially, we’d like to place a ceiling on total credits tied to the committed monthly minimum (not unlimited). We can define this as either 100% of the committed monthly recurring revenue (MRR) for a single month or a max of three months’ MRR over 12 months (whichever is lower).
- We can expedite a tailored term sheet for Borealis; attaching a short commercial term sheet (commercial-term-sheet-B-1427.xlsx) with the proposed example numbers.

If Rajesh and team can accept the pilot cadence and the aggregate cap carveout, I’ll move the term sheet to signature. Happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

Thanks,
Aditya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: commercial-term-sheet-B-1427.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Patel <rajesh.patel@borealis.com>, aditya.rao@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2026 10:14:00 -0500
Subject: Re: SLA template variance request — uptime bands & monthly credits

Rajesh / team — I reviewed the proposed banding. A few legal redlines and clarifications we’ll include in the draft:

1) Measurement and metrics: all availability and latency measurements will be based on Redwood Console telemetry for the relevant route(s). We’ll include an example calculation table in the annex (sample month with uptime = 99.42% showing credit computation).

2) Credit mechanics: Monthly Service Credits shall be the sole and exclusive financial remedy for availability and latency failures but we are open to clarifying language that preserves limited injunctive rights for severe incidents; however, we can’t accept uncapped liability.

3) Cap mechanics: instead of an unlimited 100% single-month cap, we propose: an elevated single-month cap of 100% MRR limited to the initial 12-month pilot, with an absolute aggregate cap equal to three times the average MRR measured across a rolling 12-month window. This gives Borealis runway for early issues while protecting Redwood from open-ended exposure.

4) Transparency and audits: Borealis will have access to the same SLO dashboards; for disputes we’ll provide a measurement export. For a formal audit request (beyond dashboard exports) we’ll limit to one paid audit per 12 months.

5) Force majeure & scheduled maintenance: add explicit carveouts and a definition of scheduled maintenance (72-hour notice).

I’ll circulate a redline of the SLA variant and include explicit example calculations so procurement can validate.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: sla_variant_redline_laura.docx (docx)]

From: Rajesh Patel <rajesh.patel@borealis.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2026 12:07:00 -0500
Subject: Re: SLA template variance request — uptime bands & monthly credits

Thanks all — that direction is helpful. Two quick asks before you send the redline:

1) On the "sole and exclusive remedy" wording: our CFO legal team is uncomfortable with an absolute bar on other remedies. Can Redwood provide a compromise clause that preserves credits as the primary remedy but allows carveouts for willful misconduct or data loss?

2) For latency SLOs, can you add an explicit example illustrating combined month calculation (availability + latency) so we understand how overlapping credits apply? Ideally a worked example that shows the final invoice adjustment if both availability and latency credits would be triggered in the same month.

If possible, could you send the updated draft and the worked examples by Thursday so we can hit our procurement review on Friday?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Rajesh
